correctness.rationale: Every Condorcet-winner event is a disjoint codimension-(n-1) Boolean face. Inclusion-exclusion is exactly 1 minus the sum of the n face indicators, so nonzero Walsh sums vanish except on incident-edge stars; singleton frequencies cancel between the two endpoint faces. At each nonzero allowed frequency the magnitude is B=2^(E-n+1), while the zero multiplier is B*(2^(n-1)-n). For any projection to this character span, translation averaging preserves its range and cannot increase endpoint norm, and the unique translation-invariant projection is Fourier multiplication by 1_Omega, proving global (not just convolution) minimality. Fourier inversion gives kernel numerator 2^(n-1)H(G)+4e(G)-n²+1. Independent complete Walsh computations for orders 3,4,5 give rank 4,17,56 and exact norms 1,101/32,355/64. The n->infinity constant follows after separating the rare isolate contribution (uniformly O(n^3 2^-n)) and applying a binomial central limit theorem with uniform integrability to 4e(G)-n²+1.
